title: Custom Detection Rules in Defender XDR

header.html: 1. Manage a security operations environment (40 to 45%)
Create custom detection rules by using Advanced Hunting in Microsoft Defender XDR; manage custom detection rules in Microsoft Defender XDR
the official Microsoft SC-200 study guide (skills measured as of October 21, 2026) and Microsoft Learn

toc.title: What a custom detection rule is

html:
1What a custom detection rule is

A custom detection rule runs an advanced hunting KQL query on a schedule and, when it returns rows, raises an alert and can take response actions. You build the query in Advanced hunting, test it, then choose Create detection rule.

Permission Detail
Defender role Security settings (manage) (unified RBAC)
Entra roles Security Administrator; Security Operator (if RBAC is off in Defender for Endpoint; if on, it also needs Manage security settings)
Sentinel data Also Microsoft Sentinel Contributor
Scope Users also need device group permissions for the rule scope

2Query requirements

Requirement Detail
Time column Timestamp (or TimeGenerated for Sentinel tables)
Defender for Endpoint tables Must return DeviceId and ReportId
Other Defender tables Must return Timestamp and ReportId
Impacted assets Return identifier columns: DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountObjectId, AccountUpn, RecipientEmailAddress and so on
Do not Filter on Timestamp; the service pre-filters by the lookback period

If a query uses summarize, project the columns the rule needs, because aggregation drops them.

Exam tip

. A rule query must return ReportId (and DeviceId for endpoint tables) or it cannot be saved.

3Frequency and lookback

Frequency Lookback of Defender XDR data
Every 24 hours 30 days
Every 12 hours 48 hours
Every 3 hours 12 hours
Every hour 4 hours
Continuous (NRT) Near real time
Custom Sentinel-only data; 5 minutes to 14 days

On save, the rule checks the past 30 days.

Continuous (NRT) rules need a query on one table only: no joins, no unions, no externaldata, and no comment lines. Supported tables include DeviceEvents, DeviceProcessEvents, EmailEvents, IdentityLogonEvents, CloudAppEvents, AlertEvidence.

Limit Value
Alerts per rule per run 150
Custom details 20 key-value pairs, 4 KB combined per alert
Dynamic title or description 3 columns per field
Exam tip

. Fastest detection = Continuous (NRT), but one table, no joins. If you need a join, use hourly or slower.

4Alert details and scope

You set the alert title, severity, category, MITRE techniques, description and recommended actions; the impacted entities (device, user, mailbox) come from the query columns. Scope: All devices or Specific device groups (this affects only device-based rules).

5Response actions

Group Actions Needs
Device Isolate device, Collect investigation package, Run antivirus scan, Initiate investigation, Restrict app execution DeviceId
File Allow or Block; Quarantine file A file ID such as SHA1 or SHA256; Remediate permission
User Mark user as compromised (sets Entra risk to high); Disable user; Reset user authentication AccountObjectId; SID columns for disable and reset
Email Move to mailbox folder (Junk, Inbox, Deleted items); Delete email (Soft delete or Hard delete) NetworkMessageId and RecipientEmailAddress
Exam tip

. Actions need the right columns. A user action needs an account identifier; an email action needs NetworkMessageId and RecipientEmailAddress.

6Managing rules

Path: Hunting > Custom detection rules.

Item Detail
List columns Last run, Last run status, Next run, Status
Rule page Run, Edit, Modify query, Turn on / Turn off, Delete (deleting turns the rule off and removes it permanently), Include or exclude from correlation
Sections Triggered alerts and Triggered actions

Custom detection alerts join the incident queue and are correlated with other alerts, unless the rule is excluded from correlation.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A SOC wants a detection that fires within minutes of a suspicious process starting on endpoints. Which frequency fits, and what is the limit?

  • AEvery 24 hours, with a lookback of 30 days for all data
  • BEvery 12 hours, with a lookback of 48 hours for all data
  • CContinuous (NRT), with a query on a single table without joins
  • DEvery hour, with a query that unions several different tables together
Show the answer

Answer: C. Continuous (NRT) runs in near real time but allows only one table and no joins or unions.

S2An analyst writes a hunting query for DeviceProcessEvents with summarize and tries to create a rule, but saving fails. What is the likely cause?

  • AThe query returns too few rows to build an alert
  • BThe query does not return the required DeviceId and ReportId columns
  • CThe query uses a table that is not in advanced hunting
  • DThe query was tested for fewer than seven days
Show the answer

Answer: B. Endpoint rule queries must return DeviceId and ReportId; summarize can drop them.

S3A user must create custom detection rules in Defender XDR with the least privilege and no Sentinel data. Which permission fits?

  • AMicrosoft Sentinel Reader on the workspace
  • BGlobal Reader in the Microsoft Entra tenant
  • CSecurity settings (manage), or Security Administrator in Entra
  • DSecurity data basics (read) in the security operations permission group
Show the answer

Answer: C. Creating rules needs Security settings (manage) or the Security Administrator role.

S4A rule must disable a user account when it fires. Which column requirement applies?

  • AThe query must return NetworkMessageId for the user
  • BThe query must return a SHA256 hash of the file
  • CThe query must return the account SID columns
  • DThe query must return the device group of the user
Show the answer

Answer: C. Disable user and reset authentication need SID columns in addition to the account identifier.

S5A rule returns 400 matching rows in one run. How many alerts does the rule generate for that run?

  • A400 alerts, one for each returned row
  • B20 alerts, the limit for custom details
  • C150 alerts, the limit per rule per run
  • D1 alert, because rules always group the rows
Show the answer

Answer: C. A rule generates at most 150 alerts per run.

S6A rule runs every 24 hours. How much Defender XDR data does each run look back over?

  • AThe last 48 hours of data
  • BThe last 12 hours of data
  • CThe last 4 hours of data
  • DThe last 30 days of data
Show the answer

Answer: D. A 24-hour frequency uses a 30-day lookback; 12 hours uses 48 hours, 3 hours uses 12 hours and hourly uses 4 hours.

7.2 Recall questions

R1Where are custom detection rules managed?

Show the answer

Hunting > Custom detection rules.

R2What is the maximum number of alerts per rule per run?

Show the answer

150.

R3Which frequency is near real time?

Show the answer

Continuous (NRT).

R4Which columns must endpoint rule queries return?

Show the answer

DeviceId and ReportId (with a timestamp).

R5Which file actions can a rule take?

Show the answer

Allow or block, and quarantine file.

R6What happens when you delete a rule?

Show the answer

It is turned off and removed permanently.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Permission Security settings (manage); Security Administrator
Query Timestamp, ReportId, DeviceId (endpoint tables)
Frequency 24 h = 30 days; 12 h = 48 h; 3 h = 12 h; hourly = 4 h; NRT; custom for Sentinel data
NRT one table, no joins, no unions, no comments
Limits 150 alerts per run; 20 custom details, 4 KB
Actions device, file, user, email
